family: Customs, tariff and consular/foreign service orders, 1873-1936

mechanisms.description: A port-of-entry order cited by name in the current customs regulation's list of ports (19 CFR 101.3(b)(1)) keeps operative effect: the regulation relies on it for the existence or the limits of a port that exists today.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: In force on the cutoff; the predicate is the April 1, 2025 CFR edition, with the eCFR amendment history showing no later change.

mechanisms.description: A later executive order whose words reach the member (coordinator rulings P3 and P7): it revokes, supersedes or cancels the member by number or by date and subject, or it abolishes by name the one port that was the member's only operative content.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The later order's effective date as stated in it (immediately, a fixed date, or thirty days after its date).

mechanisms.description: Spent on issue (coordinator ruling P1): an order whose only operative content abolishes or discontinues named ports of entry, or revokes or cancels another instrument, does one thing on its effective date; the consequence (the port's absence, the other instrument's end) belongs to the other instrument's or the port's history.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Order date; the held texts state effective dates up to about two months later, most often thirty days.

mechanisms.description: Merged into the parent on issue (coordinator ruling P2, from the owner's strike-and-insert ruling): an order that only amends or adds to another presidential instrument (an executive order, the Tariff of Consular Fees, the Consular Regulations of 1896, the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers) has no command of its own after issue; its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends.

One-person Foreign Service orders (coordinator ruling P4, following PD-CS-ONE-PERSON): a retirement whose own text fixes the date it takes effect ends on that date; a retirement or reinstatement without a stated date stays open.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The effective date stated in the order.

mechanisms.description: Stated maximum period: a retention on active duty for one year or for not more than five years from a stated day, or an authority to extend passports so that they are valid not more than two years from issuance, ends by its own terms when the stated period runs out.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Interval from the order date to the last day the stated period allows.

mechanisms.description: Candidate class events examined and not applied: T.D. 95-77 (1995) eliminated customs districts only 'for the most part'; EO 7968 (1938) prescribed a complete new fee tariff without naming the earlier tariff orders; EO 10718 (1957) preserved existing tariffs; Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1952 abolished collector offices, not shown to have extinguished district orders.

procedure.description: Port order cited in the current list of ports of entry (19 CFR 101.3(b)(1))

lead.basis: 19 CFR 101.3(b)(1) (April 1, 2025 edition) cites this executive order beside a port that exists today, as the order that created the port or fixed its limits; the regulation thus relies on the order's operative effect. Where the order also abolished other ports, those provisions were single acts already performed; the lead is that the order is in force at least in the provision the regulation cites.

gaps: The held CFR edition is revised as of April 1, 2025, 18 months before the cutoff; the eCFR amendment history (S2, read on the web, not held) shows no amendment of 101.3 after 2023-11-16. Acquire the eCFR text as of 2026-10-14 to close the gap.

A citation shows the regulation relies on the order; it does not show that every clause of a multi-clause order survives. Later Treasury Decisions cited beside the same port (for example T.D. 78-130 for Bar Harbor) may have redrawn part of the limits.

The match to 19 CFR 101.3 is by executive order number; for EO 5770 and EO 6284 the regulation's date (Dec. 31, 1931; Sept. 13, 1933) differs by a few days from the member date (1931-12-30; 1933-09-18) and should be checked against the order's official text.

procedure.description: Bar Harbor port created by EO 2878, abolished by EO 4572

gaps: its text continues as part of the parent (the regulations or order amended) until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

EO 7062 is flagged by the engine (acted_on_after_lead_end): EO 10000 (1948, edge SH-3647e071d203) and EO 10904 (1961, edges SH-117996891a66, SH-99fb1b72ba35) add places to the unhealthful-post list established by EO 5644 and EO 7062. Under P2 those are later events of the parent list (EO 5644 as amended), which stays open in O6; they show the list operating, not a command of EO 7062 after issue.

procedure.description: Order that only amends the Consular Regulations, the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers or the Tariff of Consular Fees

lead.basis: The order only amends or adds to paragraphs of presidentially prescribed regulations (the Consular Regulations of 1896, the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers of 1897 or 1927, the Tariff of Consular Fees). Coordinator ruling P2 covers amendments of such regulations as well as of numbered orders: the order merges into the parent on issue. The parent's later history is held at least in part: EO 5642, effective July 1, 1931, cancels and replaces Article I ('The Consular Branch of the Foreign Service'), Article II ('Retirement of Foreign Service Officers'), sections 465-473 (leave of absence) and Article XXV ('Compensation of Consular Officers') of the Consular Regulations, and the parts of the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers covering the same subjects. That reaches the text inserted by at least EO 5127 (sections 465, 467), EO 5126 (Instructions VI-5) and parts of EO 3354 (Article I paragraphs) and EO 3902 and EO 1926 (paragraphs 491-492); the list is not exhaustive and changes no lead.

gaps: its text continues as part of the parent (the regulations or order amended) until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

EO 610 is flagged by the engine (acted_on_after_lead_end): edge SH-bdbb6b2087da records that EO 2022 (1914) amends EO 610, i.e. it rewrites paragraphs 159-160 of the Consular Regulations and the Instructions that EO 610 had amended. Under P2 that is a later event of the parent regulations, not a command of EO 610.

Other held edges on B21 members are number collisions with different orders and are not used: EO 1161 (PLO 5757 revokes a Nevada land order of Feb. 17, 1903), EO 1926 (PLO 1178, partial), EO 2462 (EO 9804, partial: an order of Sept. 29, 1916 on the Employees' Compensation Act), EO 422 (EO 9951: a Hawaii order of July 23, 1930).

procedure.description: Customs collection district orders

lead.basis: Orders numbering, drawing or consolidating customs collection districts. T.D. 95-77 (1995) eliminated districts only 'for the most part' and kept them as geographical descriptions for limited purposes, so it does not show these orders extinguished. EO 4284 (abolishing District No. 33) was suspended indefinitely by EO 4299, and no later act on it is held; EO 4709 revokes EO 4337 but itself places Coos County in District No. 2, a standing assignment.

gaps: Acquire T.D. 95-77 (60 FR 50008) and any later rule abolishing customs districts outright.

procedure.description: Tariff Board and Tariff Commission orders

lead.basis: Orders organizing or funding the Tariff Board of 1909-1912 or detailing Tariff Commission staff. The Board lapsed when appropriations stopped, but no held instrument ends these orders; a lapse of funding is not an express end.

gaps: Acquire the appropriation acts of 1912 and Title VII of the Revenue Act of September 8, 1916 creating the Tariff Commission (39 Stat. 756; page of Title VII unverified) and check whether either reaches these orders.

procedure.description: Complete consular fee tariffs and standing fee directives

lead.basis: Complete tariffs of consular fees (EO 100 of 1897, EO 496 of 1906) and standing fee directives (EO 132, 2022, 2730, 3685A, 4472). EO 2022 waives passport and visa fees 'until further notice' and lets the Secretary of State terminate the waiver and restore the tariff: a standing effect, not only an amendment. No held later instrument names them by number or by an express class description (coordinator ruling P3). Disclosed earlier candidate ends, not applied: for EO 100, the complete revised tariff of EO 496, effective November 1, 1906; for EO 496 and the fee directives, the complete Tariff of United States Foreign Service Fees in EO 7968 (September 3, 1938, 3 FR 2185), which says that no fee 'will be collected for any service not covered by this tariff' but supersedes by number only 22 other orders. EO 10718 (1957) expressly preserved the tariffs then in force.

gaps: A complete replacement tariff is implied displacement under P3; an instrument naming these orders, or their class in express words, is needed.
EO 496's held text is a State Department description, not the order; EO 2730 runs 'during the continuance of the war and until further orders'.
For EO 2022, the instrument or Secretary of State action ending the waiver is not held.

procedure.description: One- or two-person retirement or reinstatement without a stated date

lead.basis: EO 4279-A and EO 4285 order named officers retired on annuity for disability without stating an effective date, and EO 7358 is a two-person order reinstating Earl L. Packer and Vinton Chapin effective on Senate confirmation, whose dates are not held. Under coordinator ruling P4 (PD-CS-ONE-PERSON) a one-person order gets a `no` lead only when its own terms fix the end or a quoted fact bounds the person's life; neither is held here.

gaps: For EO 7358, the Senate confirmation dates; for EO 4279-A and 4285, a dated fact in the order fixing when the retirement took effect or bounding the officer's life.

procedure.description: Standing Foreign Service regulations and directives

lead.basis: Standing regulations or directives for the consular and diplomatic services (appointment rules, unhealthful-post list of 1931, representation allowances, retirement-system rules, passport and visa directives). No held instrument names them by number or express class description; the Foreign Service Acts of 1946 and 1980 have not been read for provisions reaching them.

gaps: Acquire the Foreign Service Act of 1946 (60 Stat. 999) and of 1980 (94 Stat. 2071), and the Foreign Service Regulations revisions of 1941-1946, and check for express supersession of these orders.

procedure.description: Members of the administrative-orders family (PD-ADMIN)

lead.basis: These members belong to PD-ADMIN (organization of agencies, regulations, territories): EO 6778 (Federal Alcohol Control Administration acting officers, a delegation under section 2(b) of title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act; a candidate for P8 through the Act's own cessation clause, sec. 2(c), which is not held here); EO 5966 (Hoover's 1932 transfer of the border patrols to the Coast Guard, taking effect only if not disapproved under section 407 of the act of June 30, 1932); EO 2620 (Virgin Islands customs administration); EO 4353 (regulations for the Dominican customs receivership under the convention of December 27, 1924). They stay open here.

gaps: Not decided by any doctrine unless the coordinator reassigns them: the other families select members by X1 type, and these members are typed tariff_customs or consular_foreign_service.
Decide under PD-ADMIN; for EO 5966, the congressional disapproval record of January 1933 (citation unverified); for EO 4353, the 1940 convention with the Dominican Republic.

procedure.description: Members of the war and emergency family (PD-WAR-EMERGENCY)

lead.basis: EO 1960 (1914 jurisdiction over arms exports to Mexico) and EO 2017 (1914 authority of customs officers in enforcing neutrality) are war and emergency orders and belong to PD-WAR-EMERGENCY. They stay open here.

gaps: Not decided by any doctrine unless the coordinator reassigns them: the other families select members by X1 type, and these members are typed tariff_customs or consular_foreign_service.
Decide under PD-WAR-EMERGENCY.

procedure.description: Member whose held text is unreadable or is a different document

lead.basis: The held scan is illegible (EO 10, 12, 14), holds a covering letter instead of the order (EO 99), or is the State Department's description of the change rather than the order (EO 538); the summary or a description alone cannot ground a lead.

gaps: Acquire a legible copy of the order.

procedure.description: Indefinite suspensions of a port or district order

lead.basis: EO 4299 suspends EO 4284 (abolition of Customs District No. 33) and EO 5317 suspends EO 5291 (abolition of New Bern and Manteo as ports), each indefinitely. A suspension keeps a standing effect while it lasts, so it is not a pure revocation (P1); its end depends on the suspended order's lifecycle (EO 6283 later abolished New Bern and Manteo afresh without naming EO 5291 or EO 5317).

gaps: No held instrument lifts or revokes either suspension or ends the suspended order by number.

procedure.description: Port-of-entry order (creation, limits, renaming or mixed) not cited in the current port list

lead.basis: The order created, bounded, renamed or partly abolished ports. The current list of ports (19 CFR 101.3) does not cite it; the port may survive under limits redrawn by a later Treasury Decision, or may have been abolished by an order outside this family. Absence from the citation column is not evidence that the order ended.

gaps: For each port, the instrument that last fixed its limits (the T.D. cited in 101.3) or that abolished it; Treasury Decisions are not held.
EO 5291 was suspended indefinitely by EO 5317 before taking effect and the ports were abolished afresh by EO 6283, which does not name it.

EO 5577 revokes EO 5011 by number but also includes Oakland, Alameda, Berkeley, Emeryville and San Leandro within the port limits of San Francisco, a continuing port-limits provision (the San Francisco-Oakland limits now rest on CBP Dec. 06-23 under 19 CFR 101.3, which does not name EO 5577).

procedure.description: Internal revenue collection district orders

lead.basis: Orders drawing, consolidating or renaming internal revenue collection districts under R.S. 3141-3142, often designating a named collector. No held instrument shows that a later reorganization extinguished these orders; Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1952 abolished the collector offices, which may end the collector designations but has not been read.

gaps: Acquire Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1952 (66 Stat. 823) and the Treasury orders that redrew internal revenue districts after 1952; check whether 26 U.S.C. 7621 delegations superseded the presidential district orders by their terms.

procedure.description: Catch-all

lead.basis: No branch of this doctrine decides the member.

gaps: Read the order and classify it.

undecidable.reason: Indefinite suspensions (EO 4299, 5317): standing effect while they last; the suspended orders' ends are not held.
Port orders not cited in 19 CFR 101.3: the port's later history (Treasury Decisions, abolitions outside the family) is not held; EO 5577 also redraws San Francisco's limits.
Internal revenue district orders: no held instrument shows a class-wide end.
Customs district orders: T.D. 95-77 kept districts as geographical descriptions; EO 4284 suspended by EO 4299.
Tariff Board orders: lapse of appropriations is not an express end.
Complete fee tariffs and standing fee directives: later complete tariffs do not name them (P3); EO 2022's waiver runs until further notice.
One- or two-person orders without a stated effective date (P4).
Standing Foreign Service regulations: no instrument names them; the Foreign Service Acts of 1946 and 1980 not read.
Members of PD-ADMIN's subject, typed into this family.
Members of PD-WAR-EMERGENCY's subject, typed into this family.
Held text illegible, a different document, or a departmental description.
